Linfield.notes: 2023 Irish FA: GBP 7,500 for items thrown from the away end at Glentoran (Feb 2023). Dec 2023 Irish FA: GBP 4,000 for sectarian chanting and a racist comment. 2025 UEFA: EUR 10,000 plus suspended stand closure for racist/discriminatory supporter behaviour v Shelbourne.

Liverpool.notes: No UEFA/FA supporter sanction for discrimination or violence found 2021-26 (FA fines in 2023 and 2025 were for player/staff conduct, not counted); no financial-rule sanction. 2022 Paris final: UEFA-commissioned report cleared Liverpool fans.

Lorient.notes: No sanction found. LFP opened a case on supporters' pyrotechnics, chants and banners v Auxerre (March 2026), outcome not found; not counted.

Los Angeles Football Club.notes: 2023 MLS: USD 100,000 fine and 3252 suspension, for flares only (not counted). March 2025: fans brawled outside Snapdragon Stadium after the San Diego match, with no arrests and no account of who started it (not counted).

Loudoun United FC.notes: May 2021: USL investigated alleged racist chanting by home fans; outcome not found and it predates July 2021. No sanction counted.

Luton Town.notes: 2023 FA: GBP 120,000 fine and two-year action plan for homophobic chanting at Brighton (Aug 2023).

Lyon.notes: Nov 2021 LFP: one-point deduction and replay behind closed doors after a bottle hit Payet (OL-OM). Dec 2021 FFF: expelled from the Coupe de France, fined, and away fans banned after clashes and fireworks at Paris FC. Nov 2024 LFP: Lyon 1950 section closed for one match for homophobic chants v Saint-Etienne (the Feb 2024 OL-OM chant case had no outcome found, not counted). Financial: July 2023 DNCG payroll/transfer cap upheld on appeal; Nov 2024 DNCG payroll cap, transfer ban and provisional relegation; June 2025 DNCG relegation, overturned on appeal with the payroll cap kept; July 2025 UEFA settlement (EUR 50m, 12.5m unconditional); June 2026 DNCG payroll cap after change of control (single press report).

Mainz 05.notes: DFB fines 2023-24 were for pyrotechnics, tennis balls thrown onto the pitch in the investor protest, and one streaker. None involved attacks or discrimination, so none counted.

Manchester City.notes: 2020 UEFA/CAS: two-year ban for FFP breaches, overturned by CAS (July 2020) and replaced with a EUR 10m fine for non-cooperation. Sept 2026: Premier League independent commission reportedly found the club guilty on 114 of 115 financial charges; sanction pending, appeal expected, and the league has not confirmed. No supporter sanction found for 2021-26.

Manchester United.notes: July 2023 UEFA CFCB: EUR 300,000 fine for a minor break-even deficit (2019-22). No supporter sanction found. Jan 2025 Manchester disorder (39 arrests) was mainly Rangers fans and is counted there; 2025 Bilbao final clashes brought no sanction found.

Mansfield Town.notes: Sept 2024 FA: GBP 10,000 for a celebratory pitch incursion v Accrington; not an attack, so not counted.

Marseille.notes: Nov 2021 LFP: one match behind closed doors after objects were thrown at PSG players (OM-PSG, Oct 2021). Apr 2022 UEFA: EUR 98,000 and a Virage Nord closure for thrown objects and crowd disturbances v PAOK. Sept 2022 UEFA: closed-doors match and a Virage Nord closure after crowd trouble and thrown objects v Frankfurt. Oct 2023: Lyon team bus stoned, injuring coach Grosso, with arrests; no LFP sanction because it happened on the public road (counted as a documented incident). Nov 2024 LFP: suspended closed-doors match after a projectile hit a DAZN journalist. Nov 2025 UEFA: EUR 71,000 and a partial South Stand closure for projectiles and flares v Atalanta. Financial: 2022 UEFA CFCB settlement (break-even); June 2026 UEFA EUR 10m fine (football earnings plus squad cost) with a suspended European exclusion. No LFP/UEFA discrimination sanction found against OM (2022 UEFA 'provocative message' fine not counted).

Marítimo.notes: FPF fines found were for pyrotechnics, a banner, and an unregistered organised fan group. No violence, discrimination or financial-rule sanction counted.

Millwall.notes: Sept 2023 FA: sectarian chanting at Wigan's James McClean (April 2023). June/July 2025 FA: GBP 15,000 and an action plan for homophobic chants at Ben Chilwell (FA Cup at Crystal Palace, March 2025). March 2026 FA: GBP 45,000, action plan and warning for chanting referencing disability (League Cup at Crystal Palace, Sept 2025). FA charges over disability and sexual-orientation chants v Charlton (Jan 2026) are pending and not counted. No violence sanction found.

Milton Keynes Dons.notes: Dec 2022: city-centre fight outside a Peterborough pub before the match; five MK Dons fans convicted July 2023, some with football banning orders. No club sanction (counted as a documented incident).

Monaco.notes: 2022 UEFA CFCB: three-year settlement for break-even non-compliance (FY2018-22). No supporter sanction found (only individual court cases, 2023).

Monza.notes: April 2024: after Monza-Napoli, Monza ultras tried to reach a minibus of Napoli fans and attacked police with belts and sticks; the Questore issued 20 DASPO stadium bans (counted as a documented incident).

Málaga.notes: About 2021-22 FIFA: three-window registration ban over unpaid debt to goalkeeper Cenk Gonen, lifted after a settlement (exact dates unconfirmed). No supporter sanction against the club found (Antiviolencia proposals were against individual fans).

Napoli.notes: Jan 2023: Napoli-Roma ultras brawl on the A1 motorway; the Interior Ministry banned away travel for two months. Oct 2023 Serie A: EUR 25,000 for flares and bottles thrown into the away section at Lecce, injuring a fan. Sept 2024 Serie A: EUR 30,000 with a warning after smoke bombs at Cagliari injured a steward and a fan. March 2025 Serie A: EUR 12,000 for bottles thrown at Inter fans and a spit at Inter's assistant coach. March 2023 Naples clashes around the Eintracht tie were mainly Frankfurt fans (not counted).

New York City Football Club.notes: Oct 2024: MLS confirmed a spectator's homophobic slur at an NYCFC home match; no sanction (not counted).

Newcastle United.notes: June 2026 UEFA CFCB: three-year settlement for the football earnings breach (EUR 10m, EUR 3m unconditional), plus a separate EUR 3m squad cost rule fine for 2025. No supporter sanction found.

Nice.notes: Sept 2021 LFP: point deduction and closed-door matches after the Nice-OM pitch invasion in which players were attacked (Aug 2021). Oct 2022 UEFA: closed-door match after the Koln clashes (thrown objects, crowd disturbances, 39 injured). Nov 2025: about 400 ultras confronted and attacked players Moffi and Boga and an official at the training centre; prosecutors opened an aggravated-violence case (counted as a documented incident). Jan 2025 LFP: Populaire Sud closed for three matches over racist banners and homophobic chants v OM. May 2026 LFP pitch invasion v Metz (two closed-door matches) was pyro, invasion and damage, not an attack, so not counted. Financial, June 2026 UEFA: EUR 2m football earnings fine plus EUR 0.45m squad cost fine.

Norwich City.notes: Jan 2024 FA: GBP 10,000 and an action plan for disability-related chanting at the King's Lynn friendly (July 2023).

Nottingham Forest.notes: May 2023 FA: GBP 50,000 (half suspended) for the May 2022 play-off pitch invasion in which a fan headbutted Billy Sharp. Financial: 2024 Premier League PSR four-point deduction; June 2026 UEFA EUR 2.5m squad cost rule fine. The 2025 GBP 750,000 fine was for club conduct, not counted.

Oldham Athletic.notes: 2023 FA: GBP 5,000 for a celebratory pitch encroachment at Chesterfield; 2022 protest pitch invasions against the owner. Neither was an attack, so not counted.

Osasuna.notes: Feb 2026: after Osasuna-Real Madrid, about 30 Graderio Sur fans threw objects and bins at police; 13 arrested for public disorder and assault on officers (counted as a documented incident). LaLiga reports of insulting chants (incl. at Vinicius, 2024) found no confirmed discriminatory sanction, so not counted. Antiviolencia proposals (Nov 2025 EUR 75,000 for a banned fan kept as season-ticket holder; June 2026 two-month closure and EUR 200,000 over flares and ultra symbols at a training session) are not violence or discrimination.

PSV Eindhoven.notes: 2023 UEFA: reported EUR 20,000 fine and a one-match stand closure after a fan punched Sevilla goalkeeper Dmitrovic (Feb 2023); the fan was jailed and given a 40-year club ban.

Paris FC.notes: Dec 2021 FFF: expelled from the Coupe de France, fined and ordered to play five matches away from Charlety after fan clashes v Lyon (later eased on appeal). May 2025: government decree dissolved the Legion X group, which claimed to support Paris FC, for brawls causing injuries (incl. Nov 2024 after Paris FC-Rodez); the club disowned the group.

Paris Saint-Germain.notes: Oct 2023 LFP: Auteuil closed for two matches (one suspended) for homophobic chants at PSG-OM. Nov 2024 LFP: one-match Auteuil closure for homophobic chants during PSG-Strasbourg. April 2025 LFP: partial Auteuil closure and EUR 20,000 for sexist chants and banners against Rabiot and his mother. Aug 2025 UEFA: EUR 148,000 for a pitch invasion, objects thrown and fireworks at the Champions League final. Financial: 2022 UEFA CFCB settlement. Two deaths in France during the May 2025 title celebrations (a stabbing in Dax and a road accident in Paris) were not attributed to supporter violence linked to the club, so deaths = false.

Parma.notes: No supporter sanction found; the 2015 bankruptcy predates the window.

Peterborough United.notes: No club sanction found. One Peterborough fan was among those convicted for the Dec 2022 fight with MK Dons fans (counted under MK Dons).

Philadelphia Union.notes: 2026 MLS: sporting director Ernst Tanner suspended for racist, sexist and anti-gay remarks (he denies them). This is an individual staff sanction, not a club or supporter case, so not counted. No supporter sanction found.

Plymouth Argyle.notes: Nov 2024 FA: GBP 45,000 for a celebratory pitch incursion v Hull (May 2024); not an attack, so not counted.

Port Vale.notes: 2022 FA: GBP 15,000 for the pitch invasion after the play-off semi-final v Swindon, during which Swindon's Mandela Egbo was reportedly assaulted.

Portland Timbers.notes: No MLS club or supporter sanction found 2021-26.

Porto.notes: July 2022 FPF: Dragao closed for two matches and EUR 25,245 after thrown objects and staff assaults at the Feb 2022 Sporting classico (upheld by TAD in 2023). Aug 2023 FPF: fines incl. a chair thrown that hit a photojournalist at the Supertaca. Oct 2023 FPF: one closed-door match (annulled by TAD Jan 2024) and a fine for assaults after a firework from the Porto end injured two children at Moreirense. Nov 2023: Super Dragoes members assaulted club members at the general assembly; leader convicted 2025 (counted as a documented incident). Dec 2024 UEFA: EUR 20,000 and a suspended away-ticket ban for pyro and thrown objects at Anderlecht. Feb 2026 FPF: fines over EUR 35,000 incl. objects thrown at Sporting's bench. Financial: June 2017 UEFA settlement (EUR 0.7m unconditional, squad cap); July 2025 UEFA EUR 5m fine (EUR 0.75m unconditional).

Portsmouth.notes: Jan 2026: a pyrotechnic thrown at the Southampton derby injured a ball boy and burned a staff member; 12 men were charged with throwing missiles, and the FA investigation outcome was not found (counted as a documented incident). Jan 2025 FA GBP 50,000 for a celebratory pitch invasion (not counted). April 2025: a bottle thrown at an assistant referee, with no sanction found.

Preston North End.notes: May 2024 FA: one sanction covering homophobic chanting at Huddersfield (Dec 2023) and Chelsea (Jan 2024).

Queens Park Rangers.notes: July 2018: settlement with the EFL over the 2013-14 FFP breach (GBP 42m).

RB Leipzig.notes: 2023 DFB: EUR 9,500 (reduced) incl. a case where two Leipzig fans beat a Schalke fan with flagpoles (Jan 2023). Other DFB fines 2023-24 were for pyrotechnics or cups thrown at the pitch (not counted).

Racing Santander.notes: Antiviolencia proposals (EUR 200,000 and a two-month closure, among others) were for celebratory pitch invasions and flares, not attacks, so not counted.

Rangers.notes: March 2025 UEFA: EUR 30,000 and a suspended Copland Stand closure for a discriminatory banner v Fenerbahce. Jan 2025: Manchester disorder at the Manchester United match, with 39 arrests and fighting in the home end (documented, no sanction found). April 2025: Bilbao clashes with Athletic fans, about 6 arrests and 13 injured (documented). March 2026 SFA: next home Scottish Cup match behind closed doors, GBP 100,000 compensation and a suspended closure after the Ibrox Old Firm pitch disorder (37 arrests).
